content.content:
**Timeline**
- **2021:** Lacy signed with RCA Records. The song was first recorded in June 2021, using a beat he made with drums he had used before.
- **2021–2022:** Lacy reworked the song over the next year, changing the ending breakdown, the drums, and the chorus. Lacy also stated it was completed a week before he submitted *Gemini Rights* to RCA.
- **June 29, 2022:** Released as the second single from *Gemini Rights*, which came out July 15, 2022.

**Origin**
- Lacy called writing the song a turning point, saying it was "the start of this renaissance of the separation between [past] Steve and [present] Steve." ([GQ](https://www.gq.com/story/gq-hype-steve-lacy))
- After Lacy played the instrumental for Fousheé, the two freestyled over it for about 20 minutes. That session produced the verses and a chorus melody. ([The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/music/2022/dec/22/my-mom-thinks-im-doing-drugs-but-im-at-home-baking-cookies-steve-lacy-on-his-breakout-year)) The article describes this account but doesn't include a direct quote from Fousheé.

**Writing credits**
- Songwriters per the album liner notes: Steve Lacy (songwriting, production, bass), John Carroll Kirby (songwriting, additional synths), Brittany Fousheé, Diana Gordon, and Matthew Castellanos (all songwriting). ([Album booklet, *Gemini Rights*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gemini_Rights))
- Diana Gordon wrote part of the ending. ([The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/music/2022/dec/22/my-mom-thinks-im-doing-drugs-but-im-at-home-baking-cookies-steve-lacy-on-his-breakout-year))
- Kirby and Castellanos are credited as co-writers. ([Billboard lyrics feature](https://www.billboard.com/music/lyrics/steve-lacy-bad-habit-lyrics-1235118457/))
- Note: the article spells Fousheé's first name "Britanny" in the infobox and "Brittany" in the credits.

**Production, mixing, and mastering**
- Produced by Lacy. ([Billboard](https://www.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/steve-lacy-bad-habit-hot-100-sam-smith-kim-petras-glorilla-cardi-b-1235149114/))
- Mixed by Neal Pogue at his Hot Purple Petting Zoo studio in Los Angeles, and mastered by Mike Bozzi of Bernie Grundman Mastering. ([Billboard](https://www.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/steve-lacy-bad-habit-hot-100-sam-smith-kim-petras-glorilla-cardi-b-1235149114/))
- Pogue mixed the guitar riff to be the song's main focus. ([Sound on Sound](https://www.soundonsound.com/techniques/inside-track-steve-lacy-bad-habit))

**Late changes**
- Tyler, the Creator suggested altering the chorus to make it "more memorable," and Lacy adopted the change. ([Billboard Chartbreaker interview](https://www.billboard.com/music/features/steve-lacy-bad-habit-billboard-august-2022-chartbreaker-interview-1235121728/))

**Gemini Rights tracks**
Lacy describes the opening track, "Static": "That song's about going through a breakup and not trying to run away from the pain of it." He adds, "I'm not gonna run away from the pain."

Lacy says collaboration depends on "Chemistry, humor, talent." He also describes it as an ongoing relationship: "Over the years, I've learned collaboration is keeping the space open and full of jokes."

Lacy says he made Gemini Rights in a studio rather than in Airbnbs or at home, and treated the space as a personal retreat: "as a sacred place where I could just relax and decompress and only think about music."
